candidate_decisions.reason: Exact 18:27 and 18:38 anchors support a bounded expansion from partnership to replacement authority and alternate refuge; all four HFT branch traces land, with unresolved context senses attributed.
Exact 18:28 and 18:38 anchors connect the confession with opposed desire and orientation toward the Lord's face; all three traced branches land and the before/after change is distinct.
The 18:32, 18:37, and 18:38 surfaces supply a formative sequence for Rabbī; every nominated branch has an exact HFT carrier and independent trigger.
The 18:34 boast, 18:38 confession, and 18:39 comparison create a specific status-and-security contact; every asset branch lands through its exact occurrence.
The focus confession and the 18:39 entry speech provide an exact threshold, utterance, will, and strength trace, changing a general creed into corrective speech before self-credit.
The exact repetition in 18:42 after enclosure, expenditure, and collapse supplies a before/after pragmatic change; all three focus branches land together.
The failed faction and self-rescue in 18:43 followed by true authority and outcome in 18:44 independently expand the focus negation from one partner to every coalition; all six traces land.
The outlier has exact focus and 18:42 triggers plus an explicit containment boundary, so its hunter-snare sense survives as an exploratory analogy rather than replacing the theological reading.
The repeated Rabb carrier and 18:41 water-withdrawal surface provide a concrete ecological contact; the cloud and water branches remain bounded exploratory resonances.

findings.title: No substitute or side refuge
findings.claim: Within the pericope, the focus refusal of partnership extends to refusal of any replacement authority, guarantee, or alternate refuge.
findings.mechanism: The focus partnership carrier meets 18:27's replacement, other-than, and refuge occurrences, turning denial of a second deity into contextual exclusion of functions that could occupy the Lord's place.
findings.reader_payoff: The confession becomes a protection of the source of guidance and refuge, not only a statement about the number of worshipped beings.
findings.containment: The partner function is contextual and 18:27 remains its own scripture-and-refuge context; no substitute is made a lexical definition of the focus verb.

epistemic.reason: Exact surfaces and complete HFT coordinates support the relation; unresolved context branches remain attributed.

findings.title: Reoriented desire
findings.claim: The focus confession performs a self-reorientation: the speaker turns toward Allah as the governing object of desire while the eyes are drawn toward worldly adornment.
findings.mechanism: The named Allah carries worship and worshipped-referent facets; 18:28 splits desire between His face and worldly adornment, making the first-person contrast an orientation of self.
findings.reader_payoff: The line is heard as a choice of what the self faces and wants, not merely as a proposition followed by a prohibition.
findings.containment: The 18:28 material is a qualified contextual frame; it does not erase the ordinary confession or assign every surrounding command to this speaker.

epistemic.reason: Exact surfaces and HFT trace are supplied, but the speaker-level inference is legacy-unbound contextual evidence.

findings.title: Lord as former and cultivator
findings.claim: Against self-credit, Rabbī names the agency that forms the human and cultivates the provision, leaving the self no causal ownership-share in person or estate.
findings.mechanism: The focus Rabb carrier supplies step-by-step formation; 18:32 makes and plants the garden, while 18:37 creates and completes the human, joining both under one formative agency.
findings.reader_payoff: Rabbī becomes an active relation of forming, tending, and completing, so refusal of partnership also refuses self-credit.
findings.containment: The formative branch deepens the personal title; it does not replace lordship with a purely agricultural or biological definition.

epistemic.reason: Exact native anchors and a complete HFT trace support the contact; the causal synthesis remains attributed.

findings.title: Status assets as functional co-lords

findings.containment: This is a functional contextual reading, not a claim that assets are literally deities or that every possession is automatically idolatrous.

epistemic.reason: Exact native anchors and all HFT coordinates are present; the functional co-lord inference remains attributed.

findings.containment: The repetition supports a preventive and retrospective contrast without deciding that regret exhausts the later verse or that the first occurrence lacks ordinary confessional force.

findings.title: Association as a self-set snare

findings.mechanism: The focus association carrier is read through the hunter-snare facet; 18:42's enclosure, expenditure, and collapse provide closing, fastening, and terminal images for the possession analogy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader gains a concrete image of a claim to possession capturing its claimant while the ordinary theological confession remains recoverable.
findings.containment: The hunter's snare is a remote concrete branch and remains an analogy, never the lexical definition of theological association.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and 18:42 surfaces and an explicit containment note are supplied, but the branch is remote and the HFT source is legacy-unbound.
